nodes.label: OKLCH palette composition strategy (5-role: bg/surface/ink/accent/muted)
nodes.rationale: 4-color frozen palettes drift to safe defaults regardless of brief; a single OKLCH seed + model-composed 5-role palette (bg, surface, ink, accent, muted) lets the same seed serve very different moods. Seed approach won mood-fit in 3/5 empirical cases vs curated 4-color palettes and tied on the rest.

nodes.label: Bolder: Brand vs Product Distinction
nodes.rationale: In brand contexts bolder means distinctive (extreme scale, unexpected color, typographic risk); in product contexts bolder means stronger hierarchy and clarity, not theatrics, because theatrics undermine trust.

nodes.label: Animate: Brand vs Product Motion Register
nodes.rationale: Brand surfaces favor one well-rehearsed motion entrance over scattered micro-interactions, rejecting the saturated fade-and-rise-on-scroll default; product surfaces favor 150-250ms task-feedback motion with no page-load choreography since users are mid-task.

nodes.label: OKLCH palette composition strategy (bg/surface/ink/accent/muted)
nodes.rationale: Mood lives in brand colors (primary+accent) and typography, not surface; pure white/black bg defaults avoid the 'AI cliché' of warming both primary and bg. Hue-bucket inverse-frequency weighting in buildWeights ensures fair rainbow exposure despite a red/orange-skewed curated seed library.

nodes.label: Degradation table by breakpoint (Three.js, parallax, hover preview, cursor, WhatsApp button)
nodes.rationale: Below 768px, Three.js hero is replaced by a static image, parallax disabled, hover previews become tap-to-reveal, custom cursor hidden, and WhatsApp button becomes sticky bottom-right — to keep mobile performant and touch-usable.
